utterances.text: Yes, it's typical for me -- not typical, but this is much softer than man voice. And for me, I can easily distinguish this voice from the voice of the men. I didn't hear this voice anymore again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: May I put to you that there are some other possibilities. We saw a young boy in a blue shirt passing by in the video. Is it not possible that the voice belonged to this boy? And there are, indeed, men who have a very high voice. How can you exclude these possibilities?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot exclude, Your Honour. But having this picture, having this voice, and also having better-quality picture of the woman behind the bus, you know, just close to Sandici Meadow, you should be able or we should be able to recognise or just to be sure, almost, that this is a woman. But, of course, I cannot exclude that it could be a voice of the boy or -- but I think I heard this boy's voice, and I don't think that this is his.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And to follow up on the Presiding Judge's question,

utterances.speaker: MR. BLASZCZYK
utterances.text: Based on your review of the video, where is that boy that we saw in Video Still E on page 56 located at the time we see this group of people carrying this injured person up the hill and from behind the house? Where is the boy when you hear a woman's voice?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: In fact, the boy -- the boy is with another group of the people, not with this person I consider as a woman, not together with this person I consider as the woman. We saw the group of the people. We saw the man who was ordered to take out his shirt from -- T-shirt from him, and the boy is just behind him and he's in this group. This group passed already, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. And let's just roll the video for a couple more seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, we're at 23 minutes 50 seconds. What we can try to do is - it may be along the lines of the slow-motion tank video - get you some better-resolution footage.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: But is there anything, in terms of this woman's physiognomy, this person's physiognomy, that suggests to you that we're talking about a woman in this still, as opposed to a man?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is. If you look at the photo, I see the shape of the woman. You know, I see the hair of the woman. As I said, I saw the better-quality picture and I considered this person always as a woman.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. And unless she's carrying something in a pocket on her shirt, what do you see on the right side of her body or the right side of this person's body, sir?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the right side of this person's body?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Yes, in the chest area. You can say it, we're all grown-ups, Mr. Blaszczyk.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the breast.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The Chamber is of the same view.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, let's continue rolling the tape just for a couple of seconds. I don't want to overlap with what Ms. Gallagher has testified about, but let's roll and -- okay, let's keep playing, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: We've stopped at 24 minutes 10.2 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Ms. Gallagher has previously testified about this soldier and some missing footage from this version of what we call the Petrovic video that was retained in the Studio B version; specifically, some footage of a couple of dogs. The Trial Chamber may recall that the dogs are missing from this Petrovic video. My question to you, sir, about this is: Were you able to determine the location of this soldier and the soldier that's sitting next to him on this video?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, I know that these persons are sitting next to the destroyed white house, but exactly in which location, I don't know. I believe and my assumption is that this is towards on the eastern part of the destroyed white house, across the road of Sandici Meadow, but I was not able to determine the exact location where these persons are sitting.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. And in circumstances when you couldn't be so precise, did the people go in the book or did the objects go in the book or not?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I was not sure -- was not 100 per cent sure that I spotted the proper location where the object or where the people were recorded, I didn't put it in the book.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to page 60 and 61. We're drawing to the end of this chapter.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: The Trial Chamber has already seen the slow-motion footage of the Studio B Kravica warehouse execution footage, so we don't need to play it again. We'll save a little bit of time. The question for you, Mr. Blaszczyk, is: How did you make the determinations that you did on pages 60 and 61 of your road book?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we analyse the footages from Petrovic video I just have on page 60 we clearly see the shape -- the details of the warehouse depicted on these footages, and I know the location. This is Kravica warehouse. And I compare details of this warehouse -- this building from Petrovic video with details of the Kravica warehouse, itself, and I was there. And also I can say that I also supported my view of -- from the previous investigation, you know, the result of the previous investigation that was done by the previous investigator that used to work for Srebrenica case, like Jean-Rene Ruez and other of my colleagues. And if we look closely at the wall of the warehouse, and you can -- we can count even the holes of the bullets from Petrovic video. And if we look at the same -- the same wall even right now, we can count, you know, just the same amount of -- and position of the bullet-holes on the wall. And a part of that -- the part of this half road in front of Kravica warehouse is almost the same like depicted in the Petrovic video.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. And when we're looking at Video Still A on page 60, in the center of the image, just behind these bodies that are piled up there, what are we looking at, that big black-looking square?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a door, closed door, visible here as a black -- black hole here. At the beginning during our investigation, we thought at the beginning that this is open area, and two white objects over there in the middle of this page could be the reflection of the windows inside the Kravica warehouse. But after -- after making kind of experiment, that we established that it has to be door, closed door. And these two light objects in the middle of these doors are the handles of the doors. And being in Kravica warehouse several times and also in another building of this Kravica compound, I found similar doors with similar handles.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And can you point out the location in the photos that you took or are they anywhere in the photos you took on page 61 of this door that you described or these doors that you described?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am referring to the door from page -- depicted on the page 61 on my photos, on the Photos 1, just the door in the middle of the picture. Of course, it's totally different now, because we have some evidence also that -- I believe, that why the body in Kravica warehouse were removed to Kravica warehouse. Also the door and the frame of the door was destroyed at that time and then moved. And later on somebody probably put this wooden, let's say, fence or door.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Thayer, we have heard another witness who made this comparison of specific parts of this building on the video and on the pictures taken later. I think it's not necessary to repeat that again.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, and we're, in fact, done with this chapter of the road book. What I'd like to do now, very quickly, to just give another perspective, is look at P104, the map book. And we'll be looking at Maps 5 and 6 in the map book.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Judge Nyambe has a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: I just wonder if you can help me to put the Petrovic video in context. Is it my understanding that it was taken in May/June?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour. The Petrovic video was recorded in July 1995.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In two days, July 1995. This is 13 July 1995 and the following day, 14 July 1995. Only my pictures and picture of Zoran Lesic was together with UN Mission in May 2006. The only picture in this book are from this period, from May 2006. But Petrovic video, itself, the raw material and also material broadcasted by Studio B, this edited material, Petrovic material, is recorded on 13 and 14 July 1995, the entire material.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: Okay. Now, looking at your reproduction of still photos from the Petrovic video, I need to ask the following question: What are the weather conditions in the areas covered in May, June and October? October in the context of the site visit.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can say that at that time when we were there in May, and later on in June, and probably in some months later -- in fact, May, June, July, August, are more or less the same -- the same weather condition. October, the weather is going to be changed. In late September/October, the weather is going to be changed. It's getting more rainy, getting more cold, cloudy, and, of course, the leaves on the trees are changing, the colours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- in this area in this part of Europe. But, of course, in July, most of July, August, temperature in this -- in this part of Europe, in this area, is very high, very hot.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: And the trees, the trees, are they as green in July as they are in October?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Not as green as in October, but more green than October, the trees, more green. It's not getting such colour like in October. In October, the trees are getting a little bit different colour; you know, just red, brown, losing the original spring or summer colour, green.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. If we could go to page 7 in e-court, please. And if we could just scroll up a little bit. Okay. I just want to spend a second on this map and then go to the next map, just to orient ourselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: The road that we have been talking about in this last chapter extends from where to where, Mr. Blaszczyk?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were discussing the part of the road, Bratunac-Konjevic Polje, but, in fact, we were focused on that part of the road between Kravica, Sandici, and a little bit further down towards Konjevic Polje to Pervani, to Lolici and Pervani.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. And I just wanted to show this map so that we could get an idea of how these locations fit into, say, some of the more southern and northern locations, like Zvornik and Srebrenica, itself. Let's go to the next page, which is a cut-out of this same map. Okay. What I'd like you to do, Mr. Blaszczyk, is just to write in a couple of the locations that you've referred to during your testimony yesterday and today along this road, understanding that this isn't going to be scale or anything like that. But if you could fit in, if you have to use a long arrow or something like that, where Pervani is, approximately.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. And maybe on the other side of the road, you might have some more room, if you could indicate where Lolici is.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]. May I remove this? [Marks]. Okay, I --

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Just write "Lolici," if you can.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Great. Now, were you able to determine, with any precision, where along this road Mr. Borovcanin and Mr. Petrovic Pirocanac made their U-turn to head back in the direction of Sandici and Kravica?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not from the video because, as I said, the first footage, which is showing us that Mr. Borovcanin and Pirocanac, they are returning to Sandici Meadow, is visible about -- I believe about 1.000 metres from Pervani, when they recorded -- when the recordings of APC was made. And when they made the U-turn, it's not visible from -- exactly from the -- from the video. Possible that they did it in Pervani.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. And can you -- can you tell the Trial Chamber whether you think that the U-turn occurred somewhere between Pervani and Konjevic Polje, or did they do the U-turn, you think, between Pervani and Lolici? And if you don't know, if you really can't tell, that's fine, too. I just thought it might be helpful, based on looking at the locations as they are here, to give us some idea.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe that they made a U-turn in Pervani. But according to the driver of Mr. Borovcanin, I think they were -- they were on their way to Konjevic Polje, and they didn't reach Konjevic Polje. Then they made a U-turn between Konjevic Polje and sometime -- and between Sandici, but he couldn't describe exactly the location where they made a U-turn. The same, I believe, as Mr. Borovcanin in his statement, as far as I remember. But I can conclude it only based on Petrovic video.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, we need to save the document, please, Mr. President, and the Prosecution will tender it as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It will be received, this marked map.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P1345, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now -- go ahead, Mr. Blaszczyk.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: But, of course, Your Honour, I couldn't be exact -- correct with this marking. You know, just the location is more or less proper one, good one, but it's not to the scale.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Just to save a little bit of time, you've got a component of your interactive CD devoted to this chapter that we've just completed, similar to the one that you had for Potocari, with links to the various locations we've just seen, 360-degree rotation, in addition to a special portion on the Kravica warehouse. I don't think we need to spend some more time on that right now, but can you just tell the Trial Chamber what the functions are in the Kravica warehouse portion, just so you can give them a quick idea of what the capabilities are of that portion of your interactive CD.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: This Kravica portion of this presentation, we can see the Kravica warehouse, itself, my picture. And using these links, we can go inside the Kravica warehouse, we can see the entire room in Kravica warehouse, in the western part of the Kravica warehouse, and we also can be linked to the original footage from Petrovic video, I mean the footage broadcasted in the Studio B, and we can have overview, also, of most of the compound of the Kravica warehouse, itself. But the most interesting, I think, would be just to go inside the Kravica warehouse, to make a 360-degree view of the inside of Kravica warehouse, the western part of Kravica warehouse.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go back to the road book for the last two chapters, which will be much briefer than what we've already looked at. And I understand I'm five minutes shy of my one-hour estimate, Mr. President. I'm going to have to exceed that by a few minutes, but we will be moving very quickly. I think as Your Honours have probably seen from the road book, there are much fewer images to discuss, but there are a couple of things that are on the Petrovic video that didn't make it into the road book that I think would be helpful for Your Honours to hear from Mr. Blaszczyk about, in terms of where we are at certain points in the video. So when Your Honours go back and review the video yourselves, you'll have some understanding of where some of these places are.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Go ahead, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: So let's keep playing the Petrovic video. We're currently at 24 minutes 10.2 seconds in Sanction.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, the Trial Chamber's already heard about these French combat rations and what they're doing on this video. We've stopped at 24 minutes 39.6 seconds, and we are passing by what appears to be some kind of UN or UNHCR convoy. Can you tell the Trial Chamber where we are, where we're headed, and what day we're talking about here?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: We are talking about -- this is recording from the 14 July 1995, the second day of the visit of Mr. Petrovic in this Bratunac/Srebrenica area. And they are on their way from Bratunac to Potocari and then to Srebrenica and Zeleni Jadar. We are on the 14 July 1995 now. This is following day.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. And that means that they're heading south; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's correct. They are not anymore at the road Bratunac-Konjevic Polje. They are on the road Bratunac-Potocari- Srebrenica. They're heading south.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Let's play the video for about another minute.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: So we've stopped at 25 minutes 24.6 seconds. We can see the DutchBat sign on top of the building.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Again, we're in Potocari; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's correct, we are in Potocari. Mr. Borovcanin and Petrovic, they are passing by the DutchBat UN base in Potocari. They are heading towards Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And let's keep -- keep going.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And we've stopped at 25 minutes 47.5 seconds of the video.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: We can see a large amount of belongings and luggage and things along the side of the road. Again, can you tell us where in Potocari we are here?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: We are in Potocari, near the bus express compound and Jazin [phoen] factory and the blue building.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. We're just going to --

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: We seen -- we seen this location yesterday in the first chapter of this book.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And we're just a day later; correct?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is the picture -- the footage from the day later.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. We're going to roll the tape for about another 15 seconds to about 26 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: We're at 26 minutes and 1.7 seconds. The Trial Chamber, I think, with Ms. Gallagher, has already seen this portion of the footage where Mr. Borovcanin and Mr. Petrovic Pirocanac exchanged greetings with this man who's leading his horse.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, just to make it clear what's going on, I'm going to ask you a couple of questions. Based on your familiarity with the Studio B footage, what do we see on that version of the footage, that version of the Petrovic video -- right after we see this portion on this video what we refer to as the Petrovic video? What happens on the Studio B version at this point?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: On Studio B version, with edited version of Petrovic video, this footage we see on the screen right now is connected with the events in Kravica warehouse, connected with the bullets visible in the front of Kravica warehouse. In fact, as I said, this is edited material, but this is not true because this picture is taken -- or the footage is recorded on the 14 July 1995. It's mean that one day later when -- after Kravica events happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. So what we -- what we see in the Studio B version of this tape, starting at this point, is what we just saw on page 60 of your road book, is that correct, sir, just to tie it to your road book?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, you're correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And, again, what date did the Kravica warehouse mass execution take place?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Kravica -- mass execution in Kravica warehouse took place on the 13, 1-3, July 1995. This picture we see -- I see on my left-hand screen is recorded on the following day, on the 14 July --

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- and in totally different place. This is the place depicted after area between Potocari and Srebrenica, between Potocari and Gostilj. I don't remember, from the top of my head, the name of this place, but I know exactly where the place is located. I know this place.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: So how is it that this footage that we saw a few moments ago, or that we looked at in your road book, this footage of the Kravica warehouse mass execution, with the bodies in front of the door piled up, how is it that that footage, which was taken on the 13th of July, winds up in the Studio B version right next to events which were recorded on the 14th of July? How did that happen?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, the original material of Petrovic video was edited. It's mean cut off in few parts and edited in different order. This is why.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And my question is: Who did that?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was editor in Studio B.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. So, basically, Studio B chopped up the raw footage they got of the Petrovic video and put it out of order; is that another way of saying it?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Let's roll the videotape for about another minute.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Judge Mindua has a question to that. Please stop for a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Witness. I was wondering why Studio B had edited or changed the order of the images that we see.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My explanation would be that I believe this is typical for documentary, that not necessary to put everything in the order. They put in the order what seems, for them, would be the most interested for the public, just for the people who were watching the documentary, and this -- probably this is why they cut this part and they connected this part with another one, showing better -- or maybe not better, but more interested footage for the public.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Thayer, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, Mr. President. Let's roll.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I'm just going to skip a head, save about a minute or so, to 27:12. And if we could roll just a couple more frames.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. We're at 27 minutes 14.7 seconds of the Petrovic video.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber what -- where we are? We can see the letters "UN" on this building. What is this location?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: We are entering Srebrenica. This building was -- I believe it was used by UN at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. And do you know which -- which company of the DutchBat used this compound here?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, this is the building used by UN near the Dutch Company Bravo, located in Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. So Bravo Company.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Bravo Company, yes, but opposite road of the Bravo Company.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Let's just keep going for about another 10 seconds or so.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: We're at 27 minutes 24.9 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Can you tell us where we are and who these men are who are shaking hands?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: We're in Srebrenica, very close to the municipality building in Srebrenica. On the left-hand side, this is the police station, at that time the police station established by the Serbs. And on this picture, we see the deputy minister of the interior of Republika Srpska on the right-hand side, this is Mr. Tomo Kovac. And on the left-hand side, I think this policeman is called Gavric. He became kind of the head or responsible for this police station, he reporting to Mr. Kovac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Judge Nyambe, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: On the footage on the screen now, we have Mr. Tomo Kovac saying: "You didn't cover properly ... you didn't cover properly." What do you suppose he is referring to? If you don't know, it's all right.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is my assumption, Your Honour, and according to my knowledge of the situation over there. They wanted to establish the police station in Srebrenica as soon as possible because the people were coming after liberation or falling of Srebrenica, they were coming -- the people, the civilians, were coming to Srebrenica, and a lot of -- they grabbed a lot of things, you know, from Srebrenica, houses over there. They wanted to protect the public order over there.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Let's keep going, unless -- I'm sorry, Your Honour, I didn't realise you had another question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: In relation to the Kravica executions, when is this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is -- in relation to Kravica execution, this is in the following day, on the 14 of July, 1995; a day later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Let's just keep rolling the video. We'll see a sign in just a moment, and we'll freeze on the sign.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And what is this sign, sir?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is "Republika Srpska, Centar." "[Indiscernible] Srebrenica." It's written here in Cyrillic. It's the police station in Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And based on your knowledge of the events, how long had this sign been up?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since the Srebrenica was liberated. It means since 11, when the Muslims left Srebrenica and then the Serbian Army and police arrived to Srebrenica. It could be 11, could be 12.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Let's turn to page 64 and 65 in the road book. I think it's pretty self-explanatory, what we have here. Unless Your Honours have any questions about what Mr. Blaszczyk has put together on these pages, we'll just keep moving.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: You have just explained this inscription, Police Station of Republika Srpska, Srebrenica. Can you see that building here in these -- in your road book, page 64, 65?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it's not visible here, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is about a few hundred metres from the department store, Srebrencanka, heading towards Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Let's skip about 10 minutes or so to 37 minutes 38 seconds in the original timing. That would be 37 minutes 42 seconds in Sanction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It means back to the video.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay, we're right here at 37 minutes 42 seconds, and we can roll it, please. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, the Trial Chamber has previously seen footage of a single body in the middle of the street in Srebrenica, and we can see here three bodies next to each other. Can you tell us anything about these three bodies, based on your investigation?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: These three bodies are also in the center of Srebrenica, not far from -- in fact, in the center in Srebrenica. This footage was recorded by Mr. Petrovic on the 14 July 1995. But Mr. Thayer referred to -- the footage from when we see the single body was referring to the footage from 12 July 1995. I think this footage was recorded by a member of the Information Centre of the Republika Srpska. And if we go back a bit from this image, if we go to see the first body -- could we go -- could you --

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: We've stopped at 37 minutes 42.9 seconds.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This also maybe is not the best picture. But if you compare the body here, the blue jeans, the jacket, and the hair of the body, you could see that this is the same person or looks very similar as the person which body we see on the 12 July 1995 in the center of Srebrenica. I don't know, Your Honour, if you remember that when we were in Srebrenica I pointed out this place for you, where the body is lying there. This is -- for me, it's the same man. Of course, I cannot confirm for 200 per cent, but it's having the same shape, having the same jacket, having the same hair.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Let's skip ahead about a minute to 38 minutes 37 seconds. And here we are -- we see a red car approaching. If we could play this for about a minute, a little over a minute, to 38 minutes 44 seconds, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: We've stopped at 38 minutes 50.5 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I'm not sure if the Trial Chamber has heard testimony about this subject, but we see this -- somebody in the car putting up a three-fingered hand gesture. Based on your knowledge of this area and the customs and cultures, does that have any significance, this three-fingered gesture?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is sign for the victorious. We are using two fingers, for example, in my country, and the Serbs are using three fingers.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Let's skip ahead to 39 minutes 31 seconds. And here we are at that time, and let's watch about a minute of the video. And if you would, pay attention to the patch on the left arm of the soldier in the middle of these three men walking down the street.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: We've just stopped at 39 minutes 43.3 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, based on your familiarity with the various units that were operating in the area and your review of this video, have you been able to identify what that patch is on the left arm of the man in the middle?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's very visible, and even in this kind of quality footage, that this is the patch of Drina Wolves unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And what is the prominent feature on the patch of the Drina Wolves unit? And we can get a photograph of such a patch for Your Honours when the time comes, but just describe what it is.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is kind of picture of the wolf, you know, howling.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: A howling wolf?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, howling wolf.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Let's continue for another several seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: We've stopped at 39 minutes 54 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: First of all, where are we?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: We are in the center of Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And looking at this man in the center of these three men, the middle man here, we can see that there's a light blue object with some kind of badge or something on it that's folded into his belt. Do you have any idea what that is?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, this is blue beret used by UN forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Let's go forward a few more seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. We see a time and date stamp. We're at 41 minutes 6.5 seconds, and we see a time and date stamp of 14 July 1995 at 14:03 hours 36 seconds. The Trial Chamber, I think, has already heard testimony from Mr. Ruez, and it's in his book, about what happened to the mosque in Srebrenica. That was on the 30th of March, 2010. So we don't need to go into that any further.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: One final question about what we just saw. As those three men were departing, we saw that tall one, who had the UN beret that you described tucked in his belt, throw up that three-fingered salute again as they left. Is that three-fingered salute something that a Bosnian Muslim would have signaled to a fellow Bosnian Muslim?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they use two fingers. The Bosnians, they use two fingers.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: So let's go to pages 66 and 67.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: My first question is: Is this the same mosque we just saw on the video, this mosque shown in Still A?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the same mosque.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. And what is depicted in Still B? Where are we in that still, and what did you want to show here in Still B in comparison with your Photograph B on page 67?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is center of the Srebrenica. Your Honour, I don't know whether you -- you watched a few of the trial video already, and we saw that through the street, General Mladic was walking down. And I located this street, and it is located on my picture on -- on the second picture from page 67.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. And when you say this is where General Mladic was walking down the street, that's on the 11th of July?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am referring to the 11 of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: The Trial Chamber is already familiar with that footage and has seen that footage already. Okay. Now, that concludes the Srebrenica chapter of the road book. If we can turn the page to pages 68 and 69, just a couple of quick questions about the road book and a couple of questions about some locations that are on the video that didn't make it into the road book.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: You've got a map here on page 69 showing Zeleni Jadar lying on this east-west road we've heard so much about. Was there an important UN OP in the area of Zeleni Jadar? And if so, which one was it?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there is, there is important check-point of Dutch UNPROFOR in Zeleni Jadar, just in the junction, very close to this yellow dot here. I think this is Charlie, Charlie Check-point. This is check-point at -- this is kind of the border between enclave and other territory. When we are entering the enclave from Zeleni Jadar, we have to pass this check-point. In the check-point is visible also the Petrovic video a little bit. But when we were, Your Honour, on the site visit, unfortunately, there is not much visible anymore, but we were on this junction also. From this junction down, we see the factory, and we passed very quickly, but there's some bus are probably still down there.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And the Trial Chamber has also heard a number of references to OP Echo. Can you tell the Trial Chamber where OP Echo is? You've just referred to an OP Charlie or a Check-point Charlie. You may have had a flashback to Berlin, but I just wanted to find out what we're talking about here, Mr. Blaszczyk.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't mean Berlin, but this is OP Echo for sure, not Charlie.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: So we're talking about OP Echo down here in Zeleni Jadar, and we can see that this is to the south of Srebrenica. Let's pick up at 42:25, and we'll just -- we'll run it here from 42:25 for about seven seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: We've stopped at 42 minutes 35.6 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Where are we, where are we headed, and can you tell us what we see in this frame on the outside of the right-hand passenger side of this car?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: We are coming to Zeleni Jadar right now. On the right hand, we see Check-point Echo, Dutch Check-point Echo. And when we pass the check-point and down, you could see the part of the factory in Zeleni Jadar.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. And are we still talking about the same people in the car, Mr. Borovcanin and Mr. Petrovic Pirocanac?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we are talking about the same people. They are driving in the same car.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Let's keep playing just for a couple more seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: We've stopped at 43 minutes 58 seconds. And if we turn to pages 70 and 71, I think it's pretty self-explanatory, what you've shown us here, Mr. Blaszczyk, in terms of the locations.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Can you identify who the individuals are in Video Still B on page 70?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We are in Zeleni Jadar on the 14 July 1995, and in the Picture B from the page 70, on the Still B on the page 70, in front of us the first man is Tomo Kovac, the deputy minister of the interior of RS. The man following him is Mr. Dragomir Vasic. He's head of CJB in Zvornik. And the third one is Ljubisa Borovcanin, deputy commander of the Special Police Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. President, I only have a handful of questions left. We have just a little bit more footage on this chapter and then, I think, almost no questions on the last chapter, and then I'll be done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. We must have our second break now. We will resume at 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Thayer, I take it that you will finish the examination quite soon, as you indicated.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, we are reaching the end of the road, as it were.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: But if I recall correctly, you indicated, before the first break, one hour. Now we are approaching the second hour. We are in the middle of the second hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I exceeded my initial estimate by a full half an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: In fact, you indicated at the beginning of the OTP, that you needed three hours. Now you have used 6 hours and 25 minutes, just to have it on the record. Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you for that, Mr. President. We're going to just play a couple of sections here. We're at 46 minutes 26.7 seconds, and if we could just roll the video and ask you a question about something we're going to see in just a second.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: We've stopped at 46 minutes 29.4 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Can you identify what this structure is?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is part of Check-point Echo.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. And, again, when you use the term "check-point," are you referring to an observation post?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am referring to observation post -- UN observation post -- DutchBat observation post near Zeleni Jadar.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. That concludes the Zeleni Jadar chapter. Let's fast-forward a couple of minutes to 48 minutes and 14 seconds in Sanction, and roll from here, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: We've stopped a few seconds later, at 48 minutes 25 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Can you just give the Trial Chamber an idea now, at this point, where are Mr. Borovcanin and Mr. Petrovic located and where are they heading?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: They are driving from Zeleni Jadar to Srebrenica, which is a part of the Srebrenica -- they are just now a little bit above Srebrenica on the road getting us from Zeleni Jadar to Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. And if we can skip ahead to 56 minutes 54 seconds in Sanction, please. And here we are. We can start from 56 minutes 54 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. We've stopped at 57 minutes and 9.6 seconds in Sanction. If we could turn to page 72 for the last chapter, 5, the mosque, Azemina. We can see on page 73 your map indicating the location. So we can see, from this map, we are north of Srebrenica at this point. And if we turn to pages 74 and 75, we can see Video Still B on page 74 is what we have here on the screen now.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Can you tell us what your photograph -- your two photographs on page 75 depict?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: We are now in Vidikovac settlement. We are passing Srebrenica -- we passed Srebrenica. We passed the soccer field in Srebrenica. We are just in Vidikovac settlement. I depicted, in these two photos from the page 75, the mosque. In fact, it's visible, destroyed mosque here, mosque called Azemina. Why I put this mosque in this road book, I did it because -- I don't know whether you remember when Mr. Pirocanac and -- Petrovic and Borovcanin were driving towards Srebrenica on the 14 of July, there was a discussion also about a mosque also, they were discussing this particular mosque. This is quite famous mosque in Srebrenica. It was first mosque founded by private person.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. And the Trial Chamber, again, has heard some testimony, I think, from Mr. Ruez about what happened to the mosque or mosques in Srebrenica. If we can turn the page and go to 76 and 77.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And just tell us what you have here.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: On these two pages, 76 and 77, I just -- I made some picture of this mosque, in the shape how it was in 2006.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: May I take you back to page 74, to the Still B. We have there the mosque with the minaret which is still intact, but it appears that the building of the mosque is not intact already at that time. Is that correct? Have you any knowledge about that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it's correct, Your Honour. It's correct, Your Honour. I talked to the owner of the house next to the mosque, and he is a son of the founder of this mosque. He told that the mosque was first destroyed, I believe, in 1995, the roof, and the minaret later on, after July 1995.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. That concludes the final chapter in the road book. I just have a couple more questions for you, Mr. Blaszczyk, about the remainder of the video, some locations which didn't make it into the road book. May we start playing from 58 minutes and 37 seconds on Sanction, please, and then we're going to stop just a couple of seconds later, please. Okay. And we've started at 58 minutes 37 seconds. If we could just play it to 58 minutes 40 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And we've stopped at 58 minutes 40 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber where we are here, where Mr. Borovcanin and Mr. Petrovic Pirocanac are in their car?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Driving from Srebrenica towards Bratunac, and we are passing -- we are passing Potocari. On the left-hand side, we see -- I think this is Energoinvest company, and the following building, this is Zin [phoen] company in Potocari on the left side of the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And you identified those locations from some of the aerials yesterday, I think. Now, let's play a few more seconds to 58 minutes 52 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: What do we have here?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same -- we are in the same area in Potocari I indicated yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Let's keep playing for a couple more seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And we've stopped at 59 seconds -- 59 minutes 12 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: In this segment we just played, we saw a huge amount of luggage and baggage and then some buildings on the right. Again, could you just orient us where we are here?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: We just passed the federal building. We just passed the blue building on the left-hand -- on the left side of the road, but we didn't see this building in this footage, but partially we saw the federal building and the blue company on the right side of the road just a second ago, and we are in front of the white house, and in front of the smaller road leading us to the UN Dutch base.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. We don't need to play any more of the video. But when the Chamber plays the Petrovic video to the very end, there will be a couple of minutes showing some hills and some farmland and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Could you tell the Trial Chamber what that is footage of?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to Mr. Pirocanac, this is footage recorded by him when he left -- when he left Bosnia-Herzegovina on this day, 14 of July 1995, and this is the footage of the part of the land in Serbia already.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. And my last question for you, sir, is: Going back to the example of the Studio B version that you spoke about before, particularly the portion of the Studio B version where we saw some of the footage that was recorded on the 14th of July, when we see the man leading his horse, and Borovcanin and Petrovic talk to him through the car window, when we have that footage followed by footage from the 13th of July out of sequence, and I asked you a question about how that happened, you told us that that happened -- that was done by Studio B, that they got it out of order. Can you tell the Trial Chamber, did Mr. Petrovic Pirocanac play any role in that chopping up of the video with the Studio B personnel?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he did. As the man who -- as the journalist who made this material, he -- of course, he played quite a significant role to edit this material for the future broadcast.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. And did he do that independently or did he do that alongside or with anybody from Studio B?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember from his statement and from his testimony, he did it together with editor from Studio B.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. That concludes my examination-in-chief, Mr. President. We have a couple of exhibits to tender that were on our exhibit list. The first is 65 ter 1379. That is the BBC version of the Petrovic video you heard Mr. Blaszczyk talk about and how it was better quality, in some respects, and was used to help with some of the transcripts because of its better quality. So we would tender that at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P1346, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Additionally, the Prosecution would tender 65 ter 2176, which are the transcripts for the video which we have been watching these last couple of days, the Petrovic video itself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It will be received too.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P1347, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And we also have 65 ter 2181, which is a copy of the -- another copy of the Petrovic video that was obtained from the BiH Ministry of Defence that Mr. Blaszczyk talked about obtaining and then the OTP reviewing. We would tender that as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Yes, this one as well.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P1348, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And, finally, the Prosecution would tender 65 ter 1413, which is the video, itself, the copy that the OTP made of Mr. Petrovic's eight-millimetre tape that he furnished to us during the interview in February 2006, V000-6747.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It will be received as well.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P1349, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Again, I thank the Court for its patience during this much longer examination than predicted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Thayer. We have to discuss the length of examination-in-chief in future. Mr. Tolimir, your cross-examination. Please commence your examination.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I wish to greet everyone present. May there be peace in this house, and may the outcome be as God wishes and not as I wish. We thank Mr. Thayer and Mr. Blaszczyk on the presentation of stills from the footage, which we have had the occasion to see, and their presentation. The Defence has no question about the stills, as the Defence asked Ms. Gallagher questions about the footage on the occasion of her testimony, when the footage was also presented. The Defence believes that it is not necessary to waste any further time. Thank you. Thank you, Mr. President, and thank you to everyone else in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Tolimir. Do I understand you correctly, that you have no cross-examination for this witness related to the road book and to the video we have seen related to this road book?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right, Mr. President. We have no questions because we asked the questions while we were watching the footage which was shown during Ms. Gallagher's testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Blaszczyk, you will be pleased to hear that this concludes this part of your examination. I think there are still some remaining parts in cross-examination, but you will be called again at a later stage. But for now, related to this part of your examination, you are free to return to your normal activities. Thank you very much that you were able to provide us with your knowledge.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Thayer, what's the situation?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, Mr. Vanderpuye has been monitoring the situation. I think he's on his way down with Ms. Gallagher as we speak, and he has been prepared to go today, as is Ms. Gallagher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Indeed, we should use every minute in court.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: In the meantime, Mr. President, that concludes my business before the Trial Chamber. May I be excused for the rest of the proceedings and leave you in the hands of Ms. Stewart?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Only for the rest of the proceedings of today.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We hope to see you again at another day.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Gajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, Mr. President, I apologise. On page 78, line 7, you mentioned the remaining parts of the cross-examination in connection with the testimony of Mr. Blaszczyk. We have a part of cross-examination remaining in connection with Mr. Janc, but as far as I know, we have nothing left remaining in connection with Mr. Blaszczyk.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: You see, Mr. Gajic, I'm confused sometimes because we never know which investigator has finished which part of his examination, so we have to check that. Thank you very much for your advice. Good afternoon, Mr. Vanderpuye. It's already afternoon, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. President. Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon to everyone. I understand that we've come to an abrupt stoppage in Mr. Blaszczyk's testimony, in the advent that there was no cross-examination, so I am prepared to proceed with Ms. Gallagher, who I think is in the witness room and prepared to go.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. The witness should be brought in, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Ms. Gallagher. Please sit down. I have to remind you that the affirmation to tell the truth you made at the beginning of your testimony still applies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The Chamber was discussing the question if we are still in examination-in-chief or already in cross. We are a little bit lost. Perhaps the parties can help us.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. With respect to this witness, as with previous investigator witnesses of the Office of the Prosecutor, we've had them testify in discrete sections in order to accommodate, certainly, irregularities in the scheduling and certain opportunities to present evidence as the schedule permits, and so we are, at this stage, beginning a direct examination on a very discrete area, which will be the photo identification of Bosnian Muslims that are featured in some of the video footage that comprises the trial video. And the purpose of this is, essentially, to establish the identities of these individuals and their disposition; that is, their status either as missing, or survivors, or as having been -- having been killed. And I think that will assist the Trial Chamber also to understand, basically, the process concerning the forced removal of the population, in terms of separations and in terms of what happens to some of those individuals, in addition to the survivor testimony the Trial Chamber has already heard so far.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you for that explanation. I take it that the previous sector of her testimony was already in cross-examination. I think that is correct. We had that on the 29th of October, 2010. Mr. Vanderpuye, can you give us an estimation about the length of the examination-in-chief?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I think, Mr. President, that I will not conclude the examination-in-chief today. I estimate that it would be about -- I think a little bit more an hour, hour and a half, to conclude it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Good afternoon to you, Ms. Gallagher, and welcome back. As I mentioned, I wanted to lead your examination as concerns this Bosnian Muslim photo identification project, and first I'd like to ask you: Having been assigned to the investigation of the events concerning Srebrenica, and, in particular, in relation to this case, can you tell us a little bit about this Bosnian Muslim photo identification project? Perhaps you can tell us how you and when you became involved in this project.

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I initially became involved in the project on the -- in the Popovic trial about two years ago, or I'd say in 2007. And at that time the book had already been made in 2003, and my participation was, actually, to review it, update it, make sure it was accurate, make any corrections, primarily towards to the status of the men and women that are identified in the stills and in the book. So that was briefly at that time, and it was entered in the trial not with my -- not through my testimony but as stipulated back in, I think it was, 2007. And so at that time, my involvement in the book ended. And then only recently, basically a few days ago, to review the book again, make sure that, once again, it was accurate, and to look to see if there was anything that needed to be updated, since we had new information from the ICMP in their recent list.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And can you tell us, in very general terms, what the initial objective of this identification project was, I would say, either contemporaneously with the development of the book or prior to the development of the book in the first instance?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, initially, you'll see that it started in 1996, when -- immediately when refugees were gathered in Tuzla from Srebrenica, and they were just trying to identify who was missing. So you'll see from the testimony of Pasaga Mesic, he explains taking photographs that were stills taken from these videos that we've used for the stills book and showing two refugees and trying to identify who they were. And subsequently, the ICTY then also continued the same path of trying to find out who also was missing, and more of where they were missing from, and by that time where remains were found from mass graves. So there was more investigation done by that time, the year 2000, by the ICTY.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: In terms of your objective to identify and update the status of the individuals that are depicted in the book. Can you tell us, did you rely on any particular documents, or what sources of information, I should ask more generally, did you rely on in order to do that?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I looked at, as you'll see, the statements of those that I initially identified, the photographs of the missing men, and there's one woman -- missing men and woman in the book. So I've read the statements, reviewed those, and also have looked at the ICRC missing list to make sure people are on the missing list, as well as the ICMP data, which indicated where -- when someone was identified and what grave-site they were identified at. And then I also corroborated, where I could, by looking at autopsy reports and some photographs from the exhumations or from the autopsies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Taking into account that the witness is speaking very fast, and you are using the same language, please slow down a bit and pause between question and answer, because the interpreters will not -- will have many problems.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, Ms. Gallagher, you referred to certain statements that you reviewed in order to corroborate prior identifications or identifications of the individuals that are depicted in the book. Could you just briefly tell us what the sources of those statements were? That is, apart from the individuals that gave the statements, were they attributable to any particular agency or body? If you could just tell us a little bit about that.

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: You'll see the statements coming from two different time-periods and two different sources. The first source was in 1996 by the Tuzla AID. Basically, the Tuzla police had obtained statements at that time, and those are very short ones, where they showed photographs and people identified the people from the photographs. The second source were interviews that the OTP made in 2000, June 2000. One of the investigators, Dean Manning, had done many of those interviews at that time. So mainly those two different time-periods and sources.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You made a reference to the Tuzla AID, and would that be the Agency for Investigation and Documentation?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And are those the statements that are -- well, these are the statements from 1996?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. What I'd like to show you is 65 ter 2183. All right. I think you have it on your screen now, Ms. Gallagher. While the title is pretty self-evident, it reads "Amended Bosnian Muslim Photo Identification Book." Do you recognise that?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: For the information of the Court, this is a document that was prepared, as you can see, in relation to the Popovic case. What we propose to do is to present this Trial Chamber with an updated book containing the information that Investigator Gallagher will testify to. And I will lead that evidence just now so you will understand what I'm trying to do. This document, for these purposes now, is just a demonstrative exhibit to help the Trial Chamber understand what the project is and how it has developed until now. It's an ongoing process. So I'll just continue with Ms. Gallagher, and I'll hopefully clear that up a little bit for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, Ms. Gallagher, were you involved in creating this particular iteration of the book?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was involved in this amended version; not the original version, but this -- I think it's the second version of the photo identification book.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And can you tell us, in very general terms, how this book is laid out? What does it contain and what does it show?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Initially, there's an index of all the people that have been identified in the book. Then it's split into photographs of those individuals that are listed at that time as missing. And it would be photographs -- it will be their names and a little bit of information as to how they were identified, and by who, and when, and the video that they were taken from. And then the next section is the section on survivors that have been identified. And then following that is the testimony of Mr. Pasaga Mesic. He was the chief of police in Tuzla who did the initial investigation and showing photographs to refugees and identifying people. It was a Rule 61 hearing that he testified in back in 1996. Then there's a second section attached to his testimony, which are the photographs that he used to show to people for the identifications. And then there is another supplemental amendment to that which are additional photographs that were not a part of his testimony but were used. And then I believe there are -- there's a letter, it's correspondence between Bosnia and the ICTY of those individuals that were potentially available to be identified -- excuse me, to be interviewed by the OTP. And then more correspondence in 2002 about other individuals.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. And we'll get to each of these sections as we go through the book. But, principally, how many photographs of individuals are we talking about here that we've -- that the investigation has sought to identify?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are 31 individuals, 31 photographs, that are identified in the book.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And the sources of the photographs themselves you've indicated come from certain video footage. Can you tell us what footage these photos come from? And we'll deal with them specifically when we go through the photos, but generally.

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: They come from just two video sources. One of them is the Petrovic video, which you've seen, and that is the majority of the photographs. So those come from July 13th, from his footage on that day. And then there are a number of photographs that come from July 12th, when they filmed in Potocari, and that's in some of the footage that you saw in the trial video, and that was footage we had gotten from the BBC.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, with respect to the information that was relied upon in order to identify these individuals, were you able to compare the statements that were given -- the identifying statements that were given against photographs or other documents pointing to the identity of the individuals, as compared to the photographs that are depicted in the book?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct, I've read all the statements that had been given, both in 1996 and 2000, and those are actually listed in indexes that are in the back of the book as well, and making sure that, you know, the correct photograph, the correct person, was identified.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I'd like to show you, I think it should be page 2 or 3 in e-court. All right, let's start with this one. This is okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: This, we have an index of the individuals identified. Were you involved in putting this together?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe two years ago, I may have made this index.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. And for each of these individuals, were you able to examine any statements or other indicia of identification?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. I read the statements of those that identified these 31 individuals.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Are there, in fact, statements for all of them, all of the missing individuals? Let's start with them.

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there are statements for all of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And are there also statements for the survivors that are indicated here?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in the form of -- there's several of the survivors. Whether or not statements from what we received as correspondence from Bosnia, explaining that they had been found, they were alive, living in a certain location, maybe a little bit more sometimes, but it's not a full statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And just so that we're clear, and as I mentioned, this is only demonstrative, but the eventual book will look just like this, the index of individuals identified here, you see individuals identified by "S" and individuals identified by "M." Can you tell us what is intended to express?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The "M" means "Missing." The "S" means "Survivor."

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. We'll now go to page 5 in e-court, please. And if we could just -- and we can see here this is Part 1, and this will contain information concerning individuals identified as missing. If we could go to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye, I think you are now approaching another part of the testimony. We have now reached the time for the break for today. Perhaps your last question related to this document, or will you continue on Monday?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I can continue on Monday. I'll just leave with that page. I think it's a good point to break. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We have to adjourn for the day. Ms. Gallagher, you have to continue your examination-in-chief on Monday. Please be reminded now, no contact with either party about the content of your testimony. We adjourn, and resume on Monday, in the afternoon, at 2.15 in this courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 15th day of November, 2010, at 2.15 p.m. 17 18 19 20 21 22 23 24 25
